questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The person to who I spoke was very helpful.
The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
The person whom to I spoke was very helpful.
The person to whom spoke I was very helpful.
questions.explanation: In formal style the preposition comes before 'whom'.

questions.q: The decision ___ yesterday will affect us all.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which was made' to the past participle.

questions.q: Anyone ___ left luggage should go to the office.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who leaves' to the present participle.

questions.q: The woman ___ by the window is a doctor.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who is sitting' to the present participle.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She's the friend with who I travelled to Spain.
She's the friend whom with I travelled to Spain.
She's the friend with whom I travelled to Spain.
She's the friend with whom to I travelled to Spain.
questions.explanation: The preposition stands before 'whom' in formal relative clauses.

questions.q: The money ___ in the robbery has never been found.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which was stolen' to the past participle.

questions.q: Passengers ___ to board should go to gate 12.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who wish' to the present participle.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The subject about who we argued was completely trivial.
The subject about which we argued was completely trivial.
The subject which about we argued was completely trivial.
The subject about that we argued was completely trivial.
questions.explanation: The preposition comes before 'which' for things.

questions.q: The city ___ by the earthquake has been rebuilt.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which was destroyed' to the past participle.

questions.q: He's the colleague ___ I share an office.
questions.explanation: The verb 'share with' keeps its preposition before 'whom'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The documents signing yesterday are on your desk.
The documents signed yesterday are on your desk.
The documents was signed yesterday are on your desk.
The documents sign yesterday are on your desk.
questions.explanation: A reduced passive relative uses the past participle alone.

questions.q: The house ___ in 1850 is now a museum.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which was built' to the past participle.

questions.q: Students ___ late won't be admitted.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who arrive' to the present participle.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the house in that I was born.
This is the house in which I was born.
This is the house in who I was born.
This is the house which in I was born.
questions.explanation: Formal style puts the preposition before 'which'.

questions.q: The man ___ arrested was released yesterday.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'who was arrested' to the past participle.

questions.q: The book ___ on the shelf is mine.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which is lying' with the present participle of 'lie'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Anyone interesting should apply by Friday.
Anyone interest should apply by Friday.
Anyone interested should apply by Friday.
Anyone to interest should apply by Friday.
questions.explanation: The reduced form keeps the past participle 'interested'.

questions.q: The bridge ___ the two towns was built in 1900.
questions.explanation: Reduce 'which connects' to the present participle.

questions.q: The artist ___ work I admire is exhibiting here.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession in a relative clause.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The film, directing by a newcomer, won three awards.
The film, directed by a newcomer, won three awards.
The film, was directed by a newcomer, won three awards.
The film, direct by a newcomer, won three awards.
questions.explanation: A non-defining reduced clause uses the past participle.
